public_rationale: The claim says agents cannot be built without common sense, sound reasoning, tight grounding in reality, reliable instruction-following, and enough theory of mind to infer intentions. The contract notes that 'build agents' could mean any agent or reliable general agents. The source text does not settle which. The evidence packet states that there are no agreed measures of common sense or theory of mind in agents. Without such measures, no dated event can show whether these traits are necessary. The packet considered one source, TheAgentCompany benchmark. It shows agents remained unreliable but does not test necessity, so it was not used. No evidence items are cited.
limitations: This outcome reflects the lack of agreed measures. It is not a judgment that the claim is true or false.

our_interpretation: This is a claim about what is necessary to build (by implication, capable and reliable) agents. Read literally, it is false at once, because agents of some kind were built. In context, Marcus clearly means the general, trustworthy agents he describes as years away.

The prerequisites (common sense, theory of mind, tight grounding in reality) have no agreed operational measures. A necessity claim can only be tested once a system exists that meets the target without the listed traits, and none had clearly done so or failed to do so by a settled standard.
criteria.support_condition: Not adjudicable: no observable event would show that the listed traits are necessary.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Not adjudicable in practice: refuting it would require agreed measures showing a reliable general agent that lacks common sense or theory of mind, and no such measures exist.
